chunks: Ahmad b. al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: al-Hasan b. Ali al-Sukkari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Zakariyya al-Jawhari narrated to us. He said: Abdullah b. al-Dahhak narrated to us. He said: Hisham b. Muhammad narrated to me from his father. Hisham said: And some of it was reported to me by Abu Mikhnaf Lut b. Yahya and more than one of the scholars,

regarding words that occurred between al-Hasan b. Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon him, and al-Walid b. Uqba. Al-Hasan, peace be upon him, said to him: I do not blame you for insulting Ali, peace be upon him, for indeed he lashed you eighty lashes for wine, and killed your father as a prisoner by the command of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, on the Day of Badr.

And indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, named him in more than one verse a believer, and named you a transgressor. And indeed the poet said regarding you and regarding Ali, peace be upon him: Allah revealed in the Book upon us, regarding Ali and regarding al-Walid, a recitation. So al-Walid assumed the position of disbelief, and Ali assumed the position of faith. He who was a believer worshipping Allah is not like one who was a transgressor, a traitor. Soon al-Walid will be summoned after a short while, and Ali to the recompense openly. So Ali will be rewarded there with gardens, and there al-Walid will be given humiliation.

key_terms.الْخَمْر: wine -- the intoxicant for which al-Walid was punished with the hadd penalty of eighty lashes
key_terms.جِنَان: gardens of Paradise -- the reward awaiting believers in the Hereafter
key_terms.صَبْرًا: as a prisoner -- referring to the execution of war captives, not patience
key_terms.فَاسِق: transgressor (fasiq) -- Quranic designation for al-Walid b. Uqba in verse 49:6
key_terms.مُؤْمِن: believer -- Quranic designation for Ali b. Abi Talib in verse 32:18

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Hasan say to al-Walid b. Uqba about Ali and the Quranic verses distinguishing believers from transgressors?
ai.summary: Imam al-Hasan (AS) confronts al-Walid b. Uqba, reminding him that Ali (AS) punished him with eighty lashes for drinking wine, killed his father at Badr by the Prophet's command, and that Allah designated Ali as a believer and al-Walid as a transgressor in the Quran. He then recites poetry contrasting their fates in the Hereafter.
